summary: The bad() entry point passes the unvalidated `name` request parameter straight into Runtime.getRuntime().exec(), letting an attacker inject arbitrary command tokens. The fix validates the parameter against a strict allowlist (word characters, dot, forward slash, hyphen) before it is used, rejecting any value that contains whitespace or shell metacharacters. Legitimate directory names still match and are listed exactly as before, so the directory-listing feature is preserved and no constant result is returned; only hostile inputs are refused. This follows the allowlist-on-input remediation shown in the Tomcat CVE-2019-0232 reference example. No CWE comments, scanner suppressions, test changes, or build changes were introduced.
